overview: The Community Development Board elected new officers, approved a Dover Amendment site plan for a domestic violence shelter on St. Clair Road, and approved a special permit for a second dwelling on Myrtle Street. The board also endorsed an ANR plan on Wilson Street and continued hearings for a Tufts University residence hall and the Bridal Path subdivision to February 5, 2025.

items.title: Board Officer Elections
items.summary: Emily Hedeman was elected chair and Peter Calves was elected vice chair, while nominations for board clerk were deferred to a future meeting.

items.title: 31 Wilson Street A&R Plan Endorsement (Tabled)
items.summary: The board tabled the Approval Not Required endorsement application for 31 Wilson Street until later in the meeting because the applicant was not yet present.

items.title: 401 Boston Avenue Site Plan Review
items.summary: Following an initial failed vote and a successful motion to reconsider, the board voted to continue the Dover Amendment site plan review for a proposed Tufts University residence hall to February 5, 2025, with public testimony closed.

items.title: 31 Wilson Street A&R Plan Endorsement
items.summary: The board approved endorsing the Approval Not Required plan to reconfigure three existing lots into two conforming lots on Wilson Street.

items.title: 21 St. Clair Road Site Plan Review
items.summary: The board approved a Dover Amendment site plan review with conditions for a domestic violence shelter operated by Halo House at 21 St. Clair Road, incorporating provisions for resident vehicle restrictions, shuttle service, off-street parking efforts, and a potential loading zone.

items.title: Bridal Path Definitive Subdivision Plan
items.summary: The board closed public comment and voted to continue the hearing for the eight-lot definitive subdivision off Franklin Avenue to February 5, 2025, to allow the applicant time to review and resolve engineering division comments.

items.title: 55 and 0 Myrtle Street Special Permit
items.summary: The board granted a special permit to construct a second principal single-family dwelling on the lot, with a condition requiring the preservation of existing trees on the site.
